title: Data 360 Consultant Certification - Practice Exam
description: 60-question timed practice exam mirroring the official Spring '26 Data 360 Consultant blueprint domain weights. 105 minutes, pass with 70% or higher.

questions.question: An analyst needs to explore unified profiles and build dashboards. Which Data 360 capability supports this analytics use case?
options: Connecting Data 360 data to a business intelligence tool such as Tableau
Triggering a real-time action
Publishing an activation to an ad platform
Building a match rule
questions.explanation: Analytics use cases are served by exposing Data 360 data to BI tools such as Tableau for reporting. Real-time actions and activations are action use cases, not analysis.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes RBAC from ABAC in Data 360?
options: RBAC enforces row-level access, while ABAC manages feature access
RBAC governs access to features and platform capabilities, while ABAC enforces data access through policies
They are the same mechanism with different names
ABAC applies only to unstructured data
questions.explanation: RBAC controls who can use features and admin capabilities, while ABAC enforces object, field, and row-level data access plus masking through policies. Reversing them is the classic distractor.

questions.question: A new consultant is asked to describe, in order, the stages data moves through in Data 360. Which sequence is correct?
options: Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify, Analyze and Act
Harmonize and Unify, Connect Data, Analyze and Act
Analyze and Act, Connect Data, Harmonize and Unify
Connect Data, Analyze and Act, Harmonize and Unify
questions.explanation: Data always starts with Connect Data, then Harmonize and Unify, then Analyze and Act. The strongest distractor swaps the first two steps, but you cannot harmonize data that has not been connected.

questions.question: Which prerequisite most often blocks an initial use case from working?
options: The org has too many users
The unifying entity is not mapped and unified, so the profile does not exist
The data is stored in a data lake
The segment has too few members
questions.explanation: Use cases built on profiles or segments require the entity, Individual or Account, to be mapped to the Customer 360 Data Model and unified. Data location does not block Data 360, which handles lakes through federation.

questions.question: Which capability lets a no-code admin build a predictive model using Data 360 data with clicks rather than code?
options: Bring Your Own Model
Model Builder
Retrieval augmented generation
Streaming data transform
questions.explanation: Model Builder builds and trains a predictive model with clicks using Data 360 data. Bring Your Own Model connects an already-built external model, which still requires external data science work.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Bring Your Own Model in AI Models?
options: It retrains external models inside Data 360
It runs inference against an externally trained model, exposing harmonized Data 360 data without moving it
It removes the need for any data science skills
It replaces calculated insights
questions.explanation: BYOM connects an external model endpoint and exposes harmonized Data 360 data for inference without duplicating data. It does not retrain the model or remove the need for data science.

questions.question: Which statement about Data 360 consumption is TRUE?
options: Credits are unlimited once the product is licensed
Data 360 is consumption-based: actions generate usage events that consume credits by usage type
Credits are consumed only for data storage
Flex Credits cannot be used for Data 360 work
questions.explanation: Pricing is consumption-based and each action has a usage type that decrements credits. Flex Credits are interchangeable across Data 360 and Agentforce, so the last option is wrong.

questions.question: Why is it usually a mistake to try to unify every enterprise source before delivering the first use case?
options: Unification is not supported at enterprise scale
It delays time to value and consumes credits without a proven outcome
Sources from different brands cannot be unified
It forces the use of Data Cloud One
questions.explanation: Boiling the ocean delays value and burns credits before any outcome is proven. Unification does scale and multi-brand unification is possible through data spaces, so that objection is the wrong reason.

questions.question: An admin deploys a DevOps data kit but it fails with an environment parity error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The data kit was never published
The target data space name does not match the data space used when the kit was created
The kit has too few components
The user was assigned Data Cloud User instead of Data Cloud Architect
questions.explanation: DevOps kits must deploy to the same data space they were created in, and a data space name mismatch triggers an environment parity failure. The unpublished-kit distractor is wrong because an unpublished kit would not reach the deploy stage at all.

questions.question: An SFTP data stream fails with STREAM_JOB_STATUS_CANCELLED. What is the most likely cause?
options: Two consecutive jobs ran on the same data stream
A governance tag was applied to a field
The data kit was never published
The CRM object was deleted in the connected org
questions.explanation: STREAM_JOB_STATUS_CANCELLED occurs when two consecutive jobs run for the same data stream, so only one job should run at a time. The deleted-CRM-object distractor is wrong because that produces an INVALID_TYPE error on a CRM stream, not a cancellation on SFTP.

questions.question: A team masks a field that another team uses as a join key in record-level security with joins. What happens?
options: Nothing, joins ignore masked values
The join query returns no results because the key values are masked
The data graph refreshes faster
The tag is automatically deleted
questions.explanation: Masking alters the key at query time, so the join finds no matches and record-level security with joins on masked keys returns nothing. The assumption that joins ignore masking is the strongest distractor and is wrong because joins evaluate the masked value.

questions.question: An admin created a Data 360 sandbox and the connections show Inactive with no data flowing. What is the correct next step?
options: Refresh the sandbox repeatedly
Activate each connection and provide its authorization details
Reinstall the data kit package
Change the data space prefix
questions.explanation: Connections replicate without their stored credentials, so they arrive Inactive and must be activated with fresh authorization. Refreshing the sandbox is the strongest distractor and is wrong because a refresh does not carry credentials into the sandbox either.

questions.question: A team needs to promote new identity resolution and calculated insight configuration from a sandbox to production using change sets. Which data kit type must they use?
options: Standard data kit
DevOps data kit
Unlocked package
Local data kit
questions.explanation: Change sets require a DevOps data kit, which is built for sandbox to production promotion. The standard data kit is the strongest distractor and is wrong because standard kits are not supported in change set deployments.

questions.question: An admin created a data space with prefix BR1 and now wants to rename it to BR2. What is the correct statement?
options: Rename it in Data Spaces and the change propagates automatically
The prefix cannot be changed after save because it is part of object API names
Delete and recreate the space with no impact on dependent objects
Change the prefix in the Feature Manager
questions.explanation: The prefix is fixed at save because it is embedded in API names of objects that live in multiple data spaces. Deleting and recreating is the strongest distractor and is wrong because objects already depend on the space, which blocks deletion.

questions.question: Which statement about data kits is correct?
options: Data kits carry the records as well as the configuration
Data 360 metadata must be added to a data kit before it can be packaged
A single package must contain both Data 360 and non Data 360 metadata
A package can hold only one data kit
questions.explanation: Data 360 metadata cannot be packaged directly: it goes into a data kit, and the data kit goes into a package. The claim that kits carry records is the strongest distractor and is wrong because kits carry definitions, not data.

questions.question: A CRM data stream fed from an external Salesforce org started failing after a field was deleted. Where should the admin check what changed?
options: The home org's Setup Audit Trail only
The connected org's Setup Audit Trail for deleted custom field actions around the error date
The Feature Manager
The data space prefix
questions.explanation: Changes that break a stream fed by an external org are logged in the connected org's audit trail, so filter for deleted custom field actions near the error date. Checking only the home org's audit trail is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the object and field belong to the connected org.

questions.question: An architect needs to concatenate two fields and convert a text column to a date inside a batch transform. Where does that work happen?
options: In the data stream mapping
In a transform node, which groups transformations and formulas that run in sequence
In the identity resolution ruleset
In the target DMO definition
questions.explanation: A transform node groups transformations and formulas; built-in transformations include concatenation and column type conversion, and custom formulas can be added. The distractor of doing it in the data stream mapping is wrong because mapping relates fields, it does not concatenate or convert values.

questions.question: A data stream ingests insurance claims with two dates: the date the claim was created and the date its status changed. Which date should be the Event Time Field?
options: The status changed date
The claim created date
The file extract date
Either one, because the field can be changed later
questions.explanation: The Event Time Field must be a date that does not change for a record, and the created date is set once while the status changed date moves as the claim is reviewed, which can duplicate records. The file extract date distractor is also wrong because all records in the file would share it, and the field is not editable after setup.

questions.question: An architect must let a partner's Snowflake account read a harmonized profile object and a calculated insight score without loading a copy into Snowflake. What is the correct sequence?
options: Create a data stream from Snowflake and map a data model object
Create a data share with the objects, create a data share target, then link the active share to the target
Publish an outbound ETL job that writes the objects to the partner account
Enable acceleration on an existing inbound data stream
questions.explanation: Outbound collaboration is a data share linked to a data share target, which the partner then accepts. The inbound stream and the ETL job both act in the wrong direction, and acceleration only affects query latency for inbound federation.

questions.question: Which refresh mode deletes all existing data in the data lake object and replaces it with the newly imported dataset each cycle?
options: Incremental
Upsert
Full Refresh
Accelerated
questions.explanation: Full Refresh replaces the whole dataset during each refresh cycle and is the default when no other refresh setting is available. The Incremental distractor updates only data added or changed since the last refresh, so it preserves existing data.

questions.question: Which ingestion pattern is designed for large periodic loads, such as a weekly file, rather than near real-time updates?
options: The streaming pattern of the Ingestion API
The bulk pattern of the Ingestion API
A streaming data transform
A batch data transform on the source
questions.explanation: The bulk pattern accepts CSV files when data syncs happen periodically, such as daily, weekly, or monthly, while the streaming pattern handles incremental near real-time micro-batches. The streaming data transform distractor is a transformation tool, not an ingestion pattern, so it does not load the source data.

questions.question: During an incremental refresh, some records from the previous run are processed again. How should the architect interpret this?
options: As data corruption that requires a full refresh
As expected behavior, because the last few records from the previous run are reprocessed to prevent data loss
As a sign that the connector status is unhealthy
As a duplicate-key failure that must be deleted
questions.explanation: Help states that the last few records from the previous run are reprocessed during each job run to make sure there is no data loss, so this is normal. The corruption distractor is wrong because the reprocessing is deliberate, not damage.

questions.question: Which task is the best fit for a batch data transform rather than a streaming data transform?
options: Joining three objects, aggregating, and preparing an object for identity resolution on a nightly cadence
Reacting to a single event the moment it is ingested
Writing output within seconds of an abandoned cart
Serving a real-time activation trigger
questions.explanation: A batch transform is a repeatable series of operations run manually or on a schedule and is built for heavy joins and aggregation. The strongest distractor, reacting the moment an event is ingested, describes exactly the latency profile that batch cannot provide.

questions.question: A developer finishes a streaming data transform and must correct a column name in the SQL after saving. What must they do?
options: Edit the transform and save again
Delete the transform and create a new one, because streaming transforms cannot be modified after saving
Pause the transform, edit it, then resume
Change the column at the target DMO and it updates automatically
questions.explanation: Streaming transforms activate on save and cannot be changed, so the only path is delete and recreate. The strongest distractor, editing and saving again, is wrong because an active streaming transform is not editable.

questions.question: Which two capabilities together make up Zero Copy in Data 360?
options: Data federation and data sharing
Identity resolution and segmentation
Data streams and data transforms
File federation and calculated insights
questions.explanation: Zero Copy is bidirectional: data federation brings external data into Data 360 and data sharing exposes Data 360 objects outward. Identity resolution, segmentation, streams, and transforms are Data 360 features that federation can feed.

questions.question: Which approach keeps a large external dataset in its source system while still letting Data 360 query it?
options: A full refresh data stream
Data federation or zero copy with caching or acceleration
A delete file on an incremental data stream
A streaming data transform
questions.explanation: Federation and zero copy let you use the data where it lives, and enabling caching or acceleration creates an accelerated data lake object for it. The full refresh distractor physically copies all rows, which is the opposite of leaving the data in place.

questions.question: Which statement about file federation is correct?
options: It requires the external system to execute the SQL using its own compute engine
Data 360 queries the storage layer with its own query engine and the data must be in a supported open table format
It caches a copy of the data inside Data 360
It is supported by every external system on the connector list
questions.explanation: File federation uses Data 360's own query engine against external storage, which requires a supported open table format. External compute belongs to query federation, file federation is always live queried, and not all sources support it.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the unification process?
options: Match, harmonize and map, reconcile, unify
Harmonize and map, match, reconcile, produce unified profiles
Reconcile, match, harmonize and map, unify
Unify, match, reconcile, harmonize and map
questions.explanation: Unification maps sources to the data model first, matches profiles into groups, reconciles the displayed values, and then produces unified profiles and links. Reversing mapping and matching is the strongest distractor but fails because match rules can only see mapped fields.

questions.question: When is a custom Data Model Object the right choice over adding fields to a standard object?
options: Never, standard objects are fixed.
When the data is organization-specific and does not fit a standard subject area, and you also define its relationships into the model.
Whenever you need to store any new field.
Only in a sandbox.
questions.explanation: Custom objects are for genuinely distinct data that a standard subject area does not cover, and they must be wired into the model with relationships. Standard objects can be extended with fields, so 'never' and 'any new field' are both wrong, and there is no sandbox-only rule.

questions.question: A ruleset has one match rule with two criteria. When does it link two source profiles?
options: When either criterion is satisfied
When both criteria are satisfied
When the first criterion is satisfied and the second is ignored
Only when a reconciliation rule also matches
questions.explanation: Criteria within a single match rule are combined with AND, so both must be satisfied for that rule to link profiles. The strongest distractor, either criterion, would be correct only if the two criteria were split into two separate rules.

questions.question: An architect must use data already ingested in a Data Lake Object for a second Data Model Object without reloading it. What do they do?
options: Re-ingest an identical stream.
Add a second mapping from the existing Data Lake Object to the target Data Model Object.
Clone the Data Lake Object.
Query the DLO and reload it through an API.
questions.explanation: You can map an existing DLO to an additional DMO without re-ingesting, which reuses the staged data. Re-ingesting, cloning, and API reloads either duplicate data or waste effort for a result the mapping step already provides.

questions.question: A custom Data Model Object holds the right rows but never appears in segments about people. What is the most likely gap?
options: It needs a page layout.
Its relationship to Individual, and the mapped Individual ID key, is missing, so records are not tied to a person.
Custom objects cannot be used in segments.
It must be converted into a standard object.
questions.explanation: Without the relationship to Individual and a populated Individual ID, the custom object's records never attach to a person, so person-based segments exclude them. Page layouts do not apply here, custom objects can be segmented once joined, and conversion is not required.

questions.question: A marketing team wants to store each customer's email address and phone number as separate, addressable channels. Which object family fits?
options: Engagement objects
Account Contact
Contact point objects such as Contact Point Email and Contact Point Phone, linked to Individual through Party
Party Identification
questions.explanation: Each contact point object holds one channel identifier and links back to Individual, so email and phone belong in their contact point objects. Engagement objects are interactions, Account Contact is a role object, and Party Identification holds identifiers such as a license number.

questions.question: After unification, a segment shows duplicate profiles for what should be the same customer. Which modeling decision most likely explains it?
options: Too many engagement objects.
Inconsistent Individual ID formatting or keys across sources, so the same person never matched.
Too few fields on the Individual object.
The segment is scheduled at the wrong time.
questions.explanation: Matching depends on a consistently populated, consistently formatted Individual ID; small differences across sources split one person into several profiles. Object counts, field counts, and schedule do not cause duplicate profiles.

questions.question: Why is consent a first order concern in a unification design?
options: Unification encrypts source data automatically
Combining data across sources can create inferences and uses beyond the original consent, so permitted purposes and data spaces must be confirmed
Reconciliation removes records that lack consent
Consent applies only to phone numbers
questions.explanation: Because a unified profile aggregates data across systems, the combination can create inferences and uses the customer never consented to, so the consultant must confirm permitted purposes and use data spaces as boundaries. Reconciliation does not filter on consent, and consent is not limited to phone.

questions.question: A consultant is asked to explain determinism in unification. Which statement is accurate?
options: Two runs over the same source data and ruleset produce the same groupings
The result varies each run because matching is probabilistic
Determinism means the source records are permanently merged
Determinism means reconciliation rewrites every conflicting field at the source
questions.explanation: Determinism means the same input data and ruleset yield the same groupings, which makes results reproducible and auditable. The probabilistic option is wrong because fuzzy methods compare values but the ruleset logic still produces the same matches for the same data.

questions.question: Which activation membership avoids duplicate counts for a unified customer?
options: The source Individual data model object
The Unified Individual data model object
The raw data lake object
The Contact Point Email object
questions.explanation: Using Unified Individual as the activation membership counts one row per unified profile, while the source Individual object can produce duplicate entries. Data lake and contact point objects are not memberships that represent the unified customer.

questions.question: Which insight type processes high-volume batches of stored records to produce multidimensional metrics that segment criteria and personalization attributes can read?
options: Streaming Insight
Calculated Insight
Real-Time Insight
An identity resolution ruleset
questions.explanation: Calculated Insights run high-volume batches over stored data and publish measures and dimensions consumed by segments and personalization, while streaming and real-time insights work on engagement events.

questions.question: Which statement about standard versus custom Data 360 reports is TRUE?
options: A standard report can join up to four related data model objects
A custom report type can join up to four related data model objects, while a standard report reads a single object
Both report kinds write their output back to the data model objects
A standard report can only be built on a calculated insight
questions.explanation: A custom report type joins multiple related data model objects, up to four, using the lookup relationships, while a standard report is built on one object. Reports read data and present it; they never write back to the objects.

questions.question: A stakeholder needs one view that shows a Data 360 unified customer metric next to CRM pipeline. Which surface fits best without extra architecture?
options: A standard Data 360 report on the unified object, which can also include CRM pipeline columns
A Lightning dashboard with one component on the Data 360 report and another component on the CRM report
A custom report type, because only custom report types can combine two sources
A calculated insight, because it blends Data 360 and CRM data automatically
questions.explanation: A Lightning dashboard combines components driven by different reports, so a Data 360 report and a CRM report can sit in one view. A standard report reads one object, a custom report type joins Data 360 objects, and a calculated insight computes metrics inside Data 360 rather than blending in CRM data.

questions.question: A contact record must show every email engagement from across the enterprise. Which reference path fits?
options: A copy field enrichment
A related list enrichment on a DMO with a one-to-many relationship to the unified individual
The Profile API on an engagement object
A page layout change alone
questions.explanation: A related list enrichment displays a DMO with a one-to-many relationship to the Individual or Unified Individual, which is exactly many email engagements, while copy fields need a one-to-one link, the Profile API excludes engagement objects, and a layout shows only org fields.

questions.question: A calculated insight must produce one lifetime value per customer for a personalization attribute. What must the insight group by?
options: The order date dimension
The Individual dimension so each row is a person
No dimension, for a single overall total
The product category dimension
questions.explanation: Grouping by the Individual dimension yields one row per person, which is the form a profile-level metric and personalization attribute require, while category or date groupings describe groups rather than people.

questions.question: A team has trained a predictive model in AI Models, but no segment can filter on the prediction. What is the missing step?
options: Retrain the model with more features
Run a prediction job or a batch data transform to write the predictions to a Data 360 object, then segment on that field
Move the model out from under the Einstein Trust Layer
Convert the model into a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Training produces the model, but the predictions must be generated and written to a Data 360 object before any segment can filter on them. Retraining changes the model rather than where its output lives, the trust layer is not something to remove, and a calculated insight is a different Data 360 object.

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes Real-Time Insights from Streaming Insights?
options: Real-Time Insights compute results in milliseconds from each event that updates a real-time data graph
Real-Time Insights run only on mapped data lake object aggregations
Real-Time Insights replace identity resolution
Real-Time Insights are a type of copy field enrichment
questions.explanation: Real-time insights compute per event inside a real-time data graph with millisecond results, while streaming insights summarize a rolling window, and neither replaces identity resolution nor acts as an enrichment.

questions.question: Which statement about the semantic layer is TRUE?
options: A semantic model copies Data 360 data into a separate store
Semantic models define business meaning, relationships, and metrics over Data 360 objects and are reused across Salesforce
Semantic models can only be created in Tableau Desktop
Semantic models remove the need for data model objects
questions.explanation: A semantic model is first-class Salesforce metadata that records which data model objects to use, how they relate, and the business definitions on top, and it is consumed by reports, Tableau Next, and AI. It does not copy data, is not limited to Tableau Desktop, and does not replace the data model objects it describes.

questions.question: Which statement about Data Actions is TRUE?
options: A data action edits the unified profile in place
A data action sends a payload to a target such as a Marketing Cloud Engagement data extension, the core platform, or a webhook
Data actions can only target a page layout
A data action replaces identity resolution
questions.explanation: Data actions deliver payloads to configured targets such as a data extension, the core platform, or a webhook, and they do not edit unified profiles, target page layouts, or substitute for identity resolution.

questions.question: A Data 360 report is shared as a dashboard but renders empty for the recipient. What is the most likely cause?
options: Dashboards cannot display Data 360 reports
The recipient lacks access to the underlying data model object, so the component shows nothing
The report must be a custom report type
The dashboard is missing a bucket column
questions.explanation: A dashboard inherits the viewer's access to the object and fields behind each report, so a recipient without access to the data model object sees an empty component. Dashboards do display Data 360 reports, and report kind or bucket columns do not cause an empty render.

questions.question: An architect needs a Data 360 value live on a record page with no local copy. Which approach matches that requirement?
options: A copy field enrichment that syncs on a schedule
A related list enrichment that reads the DMO through its lookup
A nightly export into a custom object
A page layout change
questions.explanation: A related list reads Data 360 data live through its lookup, so no local copy is created, while a copy field, an export, and a layout change all either duplicate the value or fail to surface Data 360 data.

questions.question: A consultant must build an audience of people whose criteria rely on recent order behavior. What is the best approach?
options: Segment on Sales Order so each order becomes a member
Segment on Unified Individual and reach order attributes through relationships
Segment on a data lake object holding the raw orders
Segment on the Segment Membership object
questions.explanation: To reach people, build on Unified Individual and traverse to order data through relationships; segmenting on Sales Order yields orders, and data lake objects are not segmentable targets.

questions.question: A segment preview returns fewer members than expected. Which cause is most likely?
options: The activation target is disconnected
The lookback window or a container whose criteria override it narrowed the data range
The segment type was standard instead of dynamic
The data space is not the default space
questions.explanation: A narrow lookback window or a container that overrides it shrinks the data range and drops members; preview is available to users with the right segment and data permissions.

questions.question: Which Flow element can retrieve Data 360 data, and how is it configured?
options: A Create Records element targeting a DMO
A Get Records element with its Data Source set to Data Cloud Object
An Update Records element targeting a DLO
A screen element bound to a calculated insight
questions.explanation: Get Records with the Data Cloud Object data source reads DMOs and CIOs; Create, Update, and Delete cannot write Data 360 data, and DLOs cannot be read.

questions.question: A marketing team needs a nightly audience pushed to an advertising platform. Which mechanism fits?
options: A data share to Snowflake
An activation that publishes the segment to an external platform activation target
A copy field enrichment on the CRM record
A data action to a webhook
questions.explanation: Activation publishes a segment to an external destination; a share is for analytics query access, enrichment is inline, and a data action is event-shaped rather than an audience push.

questions.question: An activation is saved against a segment that is still processing. How may it behave?
options: It publishes instantly regardless of segment state
It can remain in an error state until the segment finishes processing
It converts the segment to a standard segment
It deletes the segment
questions.explanation: Activating a segment that is still processing can leave the activation in an error state until the segment completes, so activate from an active or published segment.

questions.question: A team cannot find a segment built by another team. What is the most likely cause?
options: The segment was automatically archived
The segment and its data are in a different data space, or the team lacks the needed permission set
Standard segments are private per user
Segments expire after 30 days
questions.explanation: Because a segment lives in a data space and requires the right permission set, a different space or a missing permission explains a segment that appears to be missing.

questions.question: Which statement about the lookback window is correct?
options: It has no effect once the segment is saved
Container criteria can specify a narrower window that takes precedence over the segment level setting
It defaults to 30 days and cannot be changed
It applies only to dynamic segments
questions.explanation: Container criteria take precedence over the segment level window; the default is 90 days and can extend to your organization maximum, and it applies to standard segments generally.

questions.question: Which statement about using Data 360 data in a flow is TRUE?
options: A flow can update a DMO directly with an Update Records element
A flow can read DMO and CIO data but cannot create, update, or delete Data 360 data
A flow can read raw data lake objects as well as DMOs
A flow must write the decision back to Data 360 before acting on a CRM record
questions.explanation: Flows read DMOs and calculated insight objects only; there is no DLO read and no Data 360 write, so the flow acts on CRM records instead.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the recommended way to design a new segment?
options: Open the data model object with the most fields and filter until the count looks reasonable
State the business goal as audience, condition, and action, then map each part to an object, criteria, and a destination
Build the largest possible audience and let the campaign team narrow it
Base the segment only on data lake objects
questions.explanation: Design begins with the goal expressed as audience, condition, and action, then maps to an object, criteria, and a destination; data-first design and unordered audiences produce unused or wrong segments.

questions.question: Which activation type cannot be published to an activation target?
options: Standard segment with standard publish
Standard segment with rapid publish
Dynamic segment
Waterfall segment
questions.explanation: Dynamic segments run by API call only, do not persist membership, and cannot be scheduled or published to activation targets; standard and waterfall segments can be published.

questions.question: A Data Cloud-triggered flow fires on an engagement-score threshold but creates a Lead with blank fields. What should you check first?
options: Whether the running user has Modify All Data
Whether the Get Records element found the harmonized profile row (correct data space and conditions) and handled the no-records outcome
Whether the raw DLO is accelerated
Whether the data share is linked to its target
questions.explanation: Blank fields usually mean the Data 360 read returned no row or the no-records path was taken; the data space and conditions of Get Records are the first thing to verify.

questions.question: A developer adds a Get Records element that reads a DMO to the Run Immediately path of a record-triggered flow, and the element errors. What is the fix?
options: Change the object to a data lake object
Move the Data 360 read to a Run Asynchronously or scheduled path and optimize the flow for Actions and Related Records
Add Modify All Data to the running user
Remove the data space from the element
questions.explanation: Reads against Data Cloud objects must run on an asynchronous or scheduled path, so the read moves off the immediate transaction; the other options do not address the path constraint.
